What to look for in motorcycle gloves

  • Knuckle and palm protection. Look for hard or moulded knuckle armour and palm sliders that resist abrasion.
  • Waterproofing. A membrane like Gore-Tex or Drystar keeps hands dry — vital for safe control in UK rain.
  • Fit and feel. Gloves should be snug with no loose fingertips so you keep full control of the levers.
  • Season-specific. Vented summer gloves and insulated winter gloves do very different jobs — many tourers own both.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on motorcycle gloves?

Our catalogue spans £19.99 to £449.99. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Five, Held, Dainese, Alpinestars, Klim, Furygan. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Do I really need waterproof kit?

In the UK, yes. Cold, wet hands and feet impair control and concentration within minutes. A waterproof membrane is one of the best touring upgrades you can make.

faq.q: How much should I spend on motorcycle gloves?
faq.a: The range spans £19.99 to £449.99. Under £150 covers the essentials for dry commuting, £150 to £400 suits most tourers, and premium picks above £400 such as the Five RFX Race add race-grade sliders, kangaroo leather and refinement.

faq.q: Do I need more than one pair of gloves?
faq.a: In the UK, usually yes. Vented summer gloves keep hands cool but offer no warmth or waterproofing, while insulated or membrane gloves are too hot in July. Most tourers run a summer pair plus a waterproof or winter pair.

They should be snug across the palm with fingertips just reaching the ends, no bunched material and no loose tips. Loose fingertips reduce lever feel and can snag. Leather beds in slightly, so choose a firm fit over a roomy one.

If you use a phone or sat-nav on the bike, yes. Conductive fingertips on models like the Alpinestars GP Plus R V3 let you tap the screen without removing a glove, though they work best on index and thumb tips.
